key_insight: The paper shows that workflow generation improves when the model learns and reasons over knowledge hierarchies, not just direct text-to-JSON output.
engineering_relevance: For visual-creation systems like ComfyUI, this approach can yield more executable, structurally coherent workflows with better node composition and higher success rates.
method: Knowledge inversion: distill real workflows into hierarchical knowledge forms, from pseudo-code and skeletons to high-level strategies.
Knowledge injection: fine-tune the model to map task descriptions to strategies and strategies to executable workflow structures.
Reversible inference + self-refinement: generate workflows and iteratively correct structural inconsistencies for coherence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments showing richer node diversity, more coherent structures, and higher execution success rates than existing methods.
watch_item: The approach depends on high-quality workflow corpora and added inference/refinement steps, which may increase system complexity and deployment cost.
